title: Biochar effects on crop yield across all crops
research_question: Does biochar application increase crop yield across crop types and soil conditions?

population.description: Field and greenhouse crops receiving biochar soil amendment

intervention.description: Biochar application to soil (any feedstock, any rate)

comparator.description: No biochar (unamended control soil, or same fertilization without biochar)
comparator.definition: Control plots receiving no biochar but same base fertilization

primary.description: Crop yield or biomass per unit area

intervention: Biochar soil amendment (any feedstock, any application rate)
typical_effect_size: +15-25% yield increase (varies widely by soil type, crop, and biochar rate)
important_moderators: Biochar feedstock (wood, crop residue, manure, sludge)
extraction_priorities: 1. CRITICAL: Treatment = biochar-amended; Control = no-biochar control (SAME base fertilization)
2. Extract EACH biochar rate × crop combination separately
3. If biochar + fertilizer vs fertilizer alone: that's a valid comparison
4. If biochar alone vs nothing: that's also valid
6. Record biochar rate (t/ha) and feedstock type
7. Record crop species and soil properties
tc_confusion_warnings: Treatment is WITH biochar, Control is WITHOUT biochar
Some studies have biochar + compost vs compost alone - extract as biochar effect
Some studies have multiple biochar rates - extract EACH rate vs control separately
Pot experiments and field experiments both valid but record experiment type
Some studies compare biochar types (feedstocks) - each vs same control

search.seed_papers_description: Ye et al. 2020 (GCB Bioenergy), Jeffery et al. 2017, biochar meta-analyses

inclusion_criteria: Primary experiment testing biochar effect on crop yield
Reports crop yield or biomass data (numeric means)
Reports treatment and control yield separately
exclusion_criteria: Only soil properties without crop data
Only reports biochar effects on non-yield outcomes (e.g., only soil carbon)

published_pooled_effect.notes: Overall +16%; higher in tropical soils (+25%) vs temperate (+10%); sandy soils (+22%) > clay (+10%); field +12%, pot +25%
